description: Gradient decomposition with CORRECT 008d config (gate_fixed_dt=2, gate_subsample_max_dt=2). Previous measurement used wrong config (gate_fixed_dt=0, gate_max_dt=8).

original_93pct_source.status: No saved measurement data supports the 105K/93% figure. It appears to be an unverified hand-written note. No 105K checkpoint exists (008d ran to 55K, 009e continuation to 112K).

analysis.conclusion: Paper claim of 'obs 93%, reward 0%, KL 7%' is NOT supported by any reproducible measurement.
analysis.correct_config_summary: With actual training config (fixed_dt=2, subsample_max_dt=2): reward dominates (38-49%), KL second (35-40%), obs lowest (16-22%). This is the OPPOSITE of the claim.
analysis.wrong_config_summary: With wrong config (fixed_dt=0, subsample_max_dt=8): KL dominates (49-53%), obs second (25-28%), reward third (22-24%). Still doesn't match 93% claim.
analysis.wrong_config_impact: Wrong config (variable dt 1-8) spreads gradient across all 8 embedding rows, while correct config concentrates on rows 1-2 only. Absolute norms differ ~10x between configs.
analysis.key_observation: The gradient decomposition is configuration-sensitive. With correct dt=1-2 subsampling, reward head gradient dominates dt_emb, suggesting dt_emb is primarily tuned for reward prediction accuracy, not obs reconstruction.
analysis.implication_for_paper: The 'obs decoder dominates dt_emb gradient' narrative needs to be revised. The actual finding is that reward and KL together dominate (~75-85%), with obs being the smallest contributor (~16-22%). This changes the theoretical interpretation of why SGS helps.
